institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go the far east. South Korea and Japan required too high grades. China seemed like too big of an culture shock for me - so I applied for Hong Kong and Taiwan.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
Hong Kong University of Science and Technology was extremely helpfull, very informative and quickly to respond to questions.
Only thing I found miscommunicated is how expensive Hong Kong is. Supermarket prices are easily doubled compared to Denmark and if you eat anywhere else than canteens and streetfoods eating out is rather pricy as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: As soon as I arrived to the university I got all the information I needed. You could receive further assistance through the buddy program of the school if needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Lots of rooms available, I think everybody who applied for rooms on campus got it.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There is a kitchen available - there is no inventory though, this you have to buy yourself.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Shared bedroom with a desk each, a mini fridge and a wash. Lots of space for storage. Shared toilets, showers and kitchen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't expect more than what we had for the price. If you want some newer rooms with more sapce, I can recommend applying for the Jockel Hall instead.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Courses are released --> You pick what you want --> First comes first.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can write the professors for questions

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Classes I had expected to take before I arrived were not available anymore. So I had to choose other things.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Easy and simple.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The general level of the academic was lower than in Copenhagen.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I loved the much more practical way used at HKUST. On UCPH you have to read hundreds of pages each semester and not using things learned before the exams. On HKUST you get small assignments every other week which is apart of your grade, forcing you to keep up to date with the stuff, which made me feel much more prepared for exams in the end and felt like I remembered much more of the things I learned.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Urban Air Pollution
Mass Balance
Energy Resources and Usage
Atmospheric Dynamics
Survey of Ocean Science

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Atmospheric Dynamics for the math lovers
Urban Air Pollution for lot of facts

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer:
Food is EXTREMELY expensive. Especially healthy food.
7-eleven jumping for going out is a must. A beer in most clubs/bars is 80-110 DKK GLASS BOTTLE

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Electronics is cheap
Food is expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was the absolute biggest and happiest surprise to anyone living at the campus. The sport facilities are great and just in your backyard. There is a team for every little niche sport and facilities for it!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I swam every 2nd/3rd day at my stay since I had a swimming pool 100m from my room.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sign up for everything in the start.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore the city and do hikes.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Hong Kong is pretty similar to other big metropols, just with a chinese twist. The Hong Kong Island and campus was not that big of cultural change. Some places in the outskirts of Kowloon is very chinese though

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Participate in things, even though you don't always have the surplus to do so.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Some foods and the way food is served was not my exact taste. Most older people are not that humble.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I love the way people just tend to sleep wherever they want to. If you are tired you can just lay down and sleep wherever you are. I found most young people very free spirited and dressing up just as they want to not following the social norms.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Nice facilities!
More nature than you would expect!
Expensive and rather poor food :-(

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You will figure out yourself

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: You just evolve as a human

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
